Chris is a Senior News Writer for Collider. He can be found in an IMAX screen, with his eyes watering and his ears bleeding for his own pleasure. He joined the news team in 2022 and accidentally fell upwards into a senior position despite his best efforts.
For reasons unknown, he enjoys analyzing box office receipts, giant sharks, and has become known as the go-to man for all things Bosch, Mission: Impossible and Christopher Nolan in Collider's news division. Recently, he found himself yeehawing along to the Dutton saga on the Yellowstone Ranch.
He is proficient in sarcasm, wit, Photoshop and working unfeasibly long hours. Amongst his passions sit the likes of the history of the Walt Disney Company, the construction of theme parks, steam trains and binge-watching Gilmore Girls with a coffee that is just hot enough to scald him.
His obsession with the Apple TV+ series Silo is the subject of mockery within the Senior News channel, where his feelings about Taylor Sheridan's work are enough to make his fellow writers roll their eyes.

The buddy-action movie has survived countless variations because there are few formulas more dependable than putting two completely incompatible people in mortal danger together. It is an evergreen formula and, with the right cast, one can become memorable or even iconic. It's even more of a treat when you see it set against the backdrop of something unexpected, like the Cold War. What could be charming about that? Well, lots.

Since premiering globally on September 4, Mayday has quickly become one of Apple TV’s biggest current movies, topping the platform’s streaming charts around the world. John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein (Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves) put a Cold War spin on the odd-couple concept with Mayday, pairing Ryan Reynolds (Deadpool) with Kenneth Branagh (A Haunting in Venice).

Set during the Cold War, the movie follows hotshot U.S. Navy pilot Troy “Assassin” Kelly after a top-secret mission over Russian territory goes disastrously wrong. Trapped behind enemy lines, Troy encounters eccentric former KGB agent Nikolai Ustinov, forcing the unlikely pair to work together if the American pilot has any hope of making it home alive.

The cast is led by Reynolds as Troy Kelly and Branagh as Nikolai Ustinov, alongside Maria Bakalova (Borat Subsequent Moviefilm) as Anna Ustinov, Marcin Dorociński (The Queen’s Gambit) as Alexander Volkov, David Morse (The Green Mile) as Harold Kelly, Louis Cancelmi (Killers of the Flower Moon), Wendy Crewson (Air Force One), and Jesse Buck (The Boys).
